question: What was our monthly revenue over the last 12 months?
definitions: Revenue = sum of order_items.sale_price for items not Cancelled or Returned, dated by order_items.created_at.
sql:
SELECT FORMAT_DATE('%Y-%m', DATE(created_at)) AS month, ROUND(SUM(sale_price), 2) AS revenue, COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS orders
FROM order_items
WHERE status NOT IN ('Cancelled', 'Returned')
  AND DATE(created_at) >= DATE_SUB(DATE_TRUNC(CURRENT_DATE(), MONTH), INTERVAL 12 MONTH)
  AND DATE(created_at) < DATE_TRUNC(CURRENT_DATE(), MONTH)
GROUP BY month
ORDER BY month
report: Lead with the total for the 12 full months and the change versus the 12 months before. Point out the best and worst months and any steady trend. Leave out the current month because it is incomplete, and say so.

question: Which product categories brought in the most revenue this year?
definitions: Revenue as in monthly-revenue. 'This year' = 1 January of the current year up to today.
sql:
SELECT p.category, ROUND(SUM(oi.sale_price), 2) AS revenue, COUNT(*) AS items_sold, ROUND(AVG(oi.sale_price), 2) AS avg_price
FROM order_items oi
JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.id
WHERE oi.status NOT IN ('Cancelled', 'Returned')
  AND DATE(oi.created_at) >= DATE_TRUNC(CURRENT_DATE(), YEAR)
  AND oi.created_at <= CURRENT_TIMESTAMP()
GROUP BY p.category
ORDER BY revenue DESC
LIMIT 10
report: Rank the categories by revenue and give each one's share of the total. Say whether a category leads because it sells more items or because its items cost more (items_sold versus avg_price).

question: Why are users in California underspending, and how do they compare to users in Texas?
definitions: Spend per customer = revenue / customers who bought in the period. Break it down into orders per customer x average order value. Use the last 12 months.
sql:
WITH sales AS (
  SELECT u.state, oi.user_id, oi.order_id, oi.sale_price
  FROM order_items oi
  JOIN users u ON oi.user_id = u.id
  WHERE oi.status NOT IN ('Cancelled', 'Returned')
    AND DATE(oi.created_at) >= DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE(), INTERVAL 12 MONTH)
  AND oi.created_at <= CURRENT_TIMESTAMP()
    AND u.state IN ('California', 'Texas')
)
SELECT state,
  COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) AS customers,
  ROUND(SUM(sale_price) / COUNT(DISTINCT user_id), 2) AS spend_per_customer,
  ROUND(COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) / COUNT(DISTINCT user_id), 2) AS orders_per_customer,
  ROUND(SUM(sale_price) / COUNT(DISTINCT order_id), 2) AS avg_order_value
FROM sales
GROUP BY state
report: 'Underspending' means lower spend per customer, not lower total revenue: a big state has more revenue simply because it has more customers. Compare the two states on spend per customer, then say which part explains the gap: fewer orders per customer, or smaller orders. Follow up with the category mix if the order value differs.

question: Why did our churn rate spike last month?
definitions: A customer churns when 90 days pass after their last completed order with no new order. Monthly churn rate = customers who churned during the month / customers who had ordered in the 90 days before the month started.
sql:
WITH purchases AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT user_id, DATE(created_at) AS day
  FROM order_items
  WHERE status NOT IN ('Cancelled', 'Returned') AND created_at <= CURRENT_TIMESTAMP()
),
last_purchase AS (
  SELECT user_id, MAX(day) AS last_day FROM purchases GROUP BY user_id
),
months AS (
  SELECT month FROM UNNEST(GENERATE_DATE_ARRAY(DATE_SUB(DATE_TRUNC(CURRENT_DATE(), MONTH), INTERVAL 6 MONTH), DATE_SUB(DATE_TRUNC(CURRENT_DATE(), MONTH), INTERVAL 1 MONTH), INTERVAL 1 MONTH)) AS month
)
SELECT FORMAT_DATE('%Y-%m', m.month) AS month,
  (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) FROM purchases WHERE day >= DATE_SUB(m.month, INTERVAL 90 DAY) AND day < m.month) AS active_at_start,
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM last_purchase WHERE DATE_ADD(last_day, INTERVAL 90 DAY) >= m.month AND DATE_ADD(last_day, INTERVAL 90 DAY) < DATE_ADD(m.month, INTERVAL 1 MONTH)) AS churned
FROM months m
ORDER BY month
report: Show the churn rate (churned / active_at_start) for the last six months so the spike is visible against normal months. Then explain it: churn in a month reflects customers who last bought three months earlier, so look at who bought then (traffic source, category, first-time versus repeat buyers). State the 90-day definition, because the business may use another.

question: Create a report for Q1 including insights and action items for Q2.
definitions: Quarters are calendar quarters. Compare with the previous quarter. Revenue as in monthly-revenue; return rate = returned items / items sold (not cancelled).
sql:
SELECT FORMAT_DATE('%Y-Q%Q', DATE(created_at)) AS quarter,
  ROUND(SUM(IF(status NOT IN ('Cancelled', 'Returned'), sale_price, 0)), 2) AS revenue,
  COUNT(DISTINCT IF(status NOT IN ('Cancelled', 'Returned'), order_id, NULL)) AS orders,
  COUNT(DISTINCT IF(status NOT IN ('Cancelled', 'Returned'), user_id, NULL)) AS customers,
  ROUND(COUNTIF(status = 'Returned') / COUNTIF(status != 'Cancelled'), 3) AS return_rate
FROM order_items
WHERE DATE(created_at) >= DATE_SUB(DATE_TRUNC(CURRENT_DATE(), YEAR), INTERVAL 3 MONTH)
  AND DATE(created_at) < DATE_ADD(DATE_TRUNC(CURRENT_DATE(), YEAR), INTERVAL 3 MONTH)
GROUP BY quarter
ORDER BY quarter
report: Structure: (1) Summary in two or three sentences. (2) Key figures for the quarter versus the previous one: revenue, orders, customers, average order value, return rate. (3) Insights: the two or three biggest movers, found with follow-up queries by category and by month. (4) Action items for next quarter, each tied to one insight. Say which year's Q1 you used if the user didn't.

question: Which categories have the highest return rate?
definitions: Return rate = returned items / items not cancelled. Ignore categories with fewer than 50 items sold, the rate is too noisy.
sql:
SELECT p.category,
  COUNTIF(oi.status != 'Cancelled') AS items_sold,
  COUNTIF(oi.status = 'Returned') AS items_returned,
  ROUND(COUNTIF(oi.status = 'Returned') / NULLIF(COUNTIF(oi.status != 'Cancelled'), 0), 3) AS return_rate
FROM order_items oi
JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.id
WHERE DATE(oi.created_at) >= DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE(), INTERVAL 12 MONTH)
  AND oi.created_at <= CURRENT_TIMESTAMP()
GROUP BY p.category
HAVING items_sold >= 50
ORDER BY return_rate DESC
report: List the categories from highest return rate down, with the overall rate for comparison. Mention the revenue lost to returns for the worst ones. Note that the data shows that items were returned, not why.

question: How has our average order value changed over time?
definitions: Average order value = revenue / number of orders, where an order is the sum of its items not Cancelled or Returned.
sql:
WITH order_totals AS (
  SELECT order_id, DATE(MIN(created_at)) AS day, SUM(sale_price) AS total, COUNT(*) AS items
  FROM order_items
  WHERE status NOT IN ('Cancelled', 'Returned')
  GROUP BY order_id
)
SELECT FORMAT_DATE('%Y-%m', day) AS month, ROUND(AVG(total), 2) AS avg_order_value, ROUND(AVG(items), 2) AS items_per_order, COUNT(*) AS orders
FROM order_totals
WHERE day >= DATE_SUB(DATE_TRUNC(CURRENT_DATE(), MONTH), INTERVAL 12 MONTH) AND day < DATE_TRUNC(CURRENT_DATE(), MONTH)
GROUP BY month
ORDER BY month
report: Describe the trend in average order value and split it into items per order and price per item, so the reader knows whether people buy more items or pricier ones.

question: How many of our customers are new versus returning each month?
definitions: A customer is new in the month of their first completed order and returning in any later month they order.
sql:
WITH purchases AS (
  SELECT user_id, DATE_TRUNC(DATE(created_at), MONTH) AS month
  FROM order_items
  WHERE status NOT IN ('Cancelled', 'Returned')
  GROUP BY user_id, month
),
firsts AS (SELECT user_id, MIN(month) AS first_month FROM purchases GROUP BY user_id)
SELECT FORMAT_DATE('%Y-%m', p.month) AS month,
  COUNTIF(p.month = f.first_month) AS new_customers,
  COUNTIF(p.month > f.first_month) AS returning_customers
FROM purchases p
JOIN firsts f USING (user_id)
WHERE p.month >= DATE_SUB(DATE_TRUNC(CURRENT_DATE(), MONTH), INTERVAL 12 MONTH)
  AND p.month < DATE_TRUNC(CURRENT_DATE(), MONTH)
GROUP BY month
ORDER BY month
report: Show new and returning customers per month and the returning share. A low returning share means growth depends on finding new buyers; suggest retention actions if so.

question: Which marketing channels bring us the most valuable customers?
definitions: Channel = users.traffic_source (how the customer first found us). Value = revenue per customer over the last 12 months.
sql:
SELECT u.traffic_source,
  COUNT(DISTINCT oi.user_id) AS customers,
  ROUND(SUM(oi.sale_price), 2) AS revenue,
  ROUND(SUM(oi.sale_price) / COUNT(DISTINCT oi.user_id), 2) AS revenue_per_customer
FROM order_items oi
JOIN users u ON oi.user_id = u.id
WHERE oi.status NOT IN ('Cancelled', 'Returned')
  AND DATE(oi.created_at) >= DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE(), INTERVAL 12 MONTH)
  AND oi.created_at <= CURRENT_TIMESTAMP()
GROUP BY u.traffic_source
ORDER BY revenue_per_customer DESC
report: Compare channels on revenue per customer, not just total revenue: a channel can bring many customers who spend little. The data has no marketing cost, so this shows value per customer, not return on spend; say so.

question: Which brands are the most profitable for us?
definitions: Gross margin = sale_price - products.cost, for items not Cancelled or Returned. Margin % = gross margin / revenue.
sql:
SELECT p.brand,
  ROUND(SUM(oi.sale_price), 2) AS revenue,
  ROUND(SUM(oi.sale_price - p.cost), 2) AS gross_margin,
  ROUND(SUM(oi.sale_price - p.cost) / SUM(oi.sale_price), 3) AS margin_pct
FROM order_items oi
JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.id
WHERE oi.status NOT IN ('Cancelled', 'Returned')
  AND DATE(oi.created_at) >= DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE(), INTERVAL 12 MONTH)
  AND oi.created_at <= CURRENT_TIMESTAMP()
GROUP BY p.brand
ORDER BY gross_margin DESC
LIMIT 15
report: Rank brands by gross margin in money, and show margin % next to it: a brand can earn a lot in total at a thin margin. This is gross margin only; shipping, returns handling and marketing costs are not in the data.

question: How are our distribution centers performing?
definitions: Per center: revenue as in monthly-revenue, return rate as in return-rate-by-category, and average days from order to delivery for delivered items.
sql:
SELECT dc.name AS distribution_center,
  ROUND(SUM(IF(oi.status NOT IN ('Cancelled', 'Returned'), oi.sale_price, 0)), 2) AS revenue,
  ROUND(COUNTIF(oi.status = 'Returned') / NULLIF(COUNTIF(oi.status != 'Cancelled'), 0), 3) AS return_rate,
  ROUND(AVG(IF(oi.delivered_at IS NOT NULL, TIMESTAMP_DIFF(oi.delivered_at, oi.created_at, HOUR) / 24, NULL)), 1) AS avg_days_to_deliver
FROM order_items oi
JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.id
JOIN distribution_centers dc ON p.distribution_center_id = dc.id
WHERE DATE(oi.created_at) >= DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE(), INTERVAL 12 MONTH)
  AND oi.created_at <= CURRENT_TIMESTAMP()
GROUP BY distribution_center
ORDER BY revenue DESC
report: Give one line per center with revenue, return rate and delivery time, and call out any center that is clearly slower or has more returns than the rest.

question: Who are our customers by age and gender, and who spends the most?
definitions: Age bands: under 25, 25-34, 35-44, 45-54, 55 and over. Spend as in state-underspending. Never show individual customers.
sql:
SELECT
  CASE WHEN u.age < 25 THEN 'under 25' WHEN u.age < 35 THEN '25-34' WHEN u.age < 45 THEN '35-44' WHEN u.age < 55 THEN '45-54' ELSE '55+' END AS age_band,
  u.gender,
  COUNT(DISTINCT oi.user_id) AS customers,
  ROUND(SUM(oi.sale_price) / COUNT(DISTINCT oi.user_id), 2) AS spend_per_customer
FROM order_items oi
JOIN users u ON oi.user_id = u.id
WHERE oi.status NOT IN ('Cancelled', 'Returned')
  AND DATE(oi.created_at) >= DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE(), INTERVAL 12 MONTH)
  AND oi.created_at <= CURRENT_TIMESTAMP()
GROUP BY age_band, u.gender
ORDER BY age_band, u.gender
report: Describe the customer mix by age band and gender, and which groups spend most per customer. Only report groups, never individuals.

question: Why did sales of Jeans drop last month?
definitions: Compare last full month with the month before. Break the change down by brand to find which ones drive it, then by price versus volume.
sql:
WITH monthly AS (
  SELECT p.brand, DATE_TRUNC(DATE(oi.created_at), MONTH) AS month, SUM(oi.sale_price) AS revenue, COUNT(*) AS items
  FROM order_items oi
  JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.id
  WHERE oi.status NOT IN ('Cancelled', 'Returned')
    AND p.category = 'Jeans'
    AND DATE(oi.created_at) >= DATE_SUB(DATE_TRUNC(CURRENT_DATE(), MONTH), INTERVAL 2 MONTH)
    AND DATE(oi.created_at) < DATE_TRUNC(CURRENT_DATE(), MONTH)
  GROUP BY p.brand, month
)
SELECT brand,
  ROUND(SUM(IF(month = DATE_SUB(DATE_TRUNC(CURRENT_DATE(), MONTH), INTERVAL 1 MONTH), revenue, 0)), 2) AS last_month,
  ROUND(SUM(IF(month = DATE_SUB(DATE_TRUNC(CURRENT_DATE(), MONTH), INTERVAL 2 MONTH), revenue, 0)), 2) AS month_before,
  ROUND(SUM(IF(month = DATE_SUB(DATE_TRUNC(CURRENT_DATE(), MONTH), INTERVAL 1 MONTH), revenue, -revenue)), 2) AS change
FROM monthly
GROUP BY brand
ORDER BY change
LIMIT 10
report: Give the overall change first, then the brands that account for most of it. Say whether the drop is fewer items sold or lower prices. Category values are capitalised in the data ('Jeans'); check exact values with SELECT DISTINCT before filtering.
